Title: March 12, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Study Session

Topic1.Title: Boulder Strong Day of Remembrance Declaration
Topic1.Summary: Councilmember Mark Wallach presented a declaration designating March 22 as the Boulder Day of Remembrance in perpetuity to honor the ten people killed in the March 22, 2021 King Soopers mass shooting. The declaration was signed by Mayor Aaron Brockett. Wallach announced a Day of Remembrance ceremony at the Boulder Museum on Sunday, March 22, from 3:30 to 4:30 p.m., open to all.

Topic2.Title: Downtown Development Authority (DDA) Formation Analysis and Initial Recommendations
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the analysis for a proposed Downtown Development Authority that would use tax increment financing to fund reinvestment in downtown and University Hill, potentially replacing the parking-focused GIDs. Under a 1% growth scenario, projected TIF revenue starts at about $300,000 in year one and grows to roughly $3 million by year 10, with parking assets and a mill levy substantially increasing borrowing capacity. Council generally supported continued refinement of the funding structure and a standalone DDA with a 1-2 year staff-supported transition, while raising questions about revenue sharing, the base year, voter eligibility, liability, staff capacity, and climate considerations. Staff plans to return in June to determine whether to refer formation and funding measures to the November ballot.

Topic3.Title: Preliminary Discussion on 2026 Ballot Measures
Topic3.Summary: Finance staff previewed potential 2026 tax ballot measures under the long-term financial strategy, noting that 68% of city revenues are dedicated and sales tax is the largest source at 35%. Options ranged from transformational changes (sales tax on services and a sales-to-property tax swap), to mid-range measures (general purpose and public realm mill levies and a residential vacancy excise tax), to structural changes (general fund debt authorization, a mill levy cap increase, and consolidating dedicated sales taxes). Following straw polls, Council chose not to pursue transformational options for 2026 and advanced the public realm mill levy, residential vacancy excise tax, general fund debt authorization, and consolidated dedicated sales tax options. Staff will return in April with a city facilities funding discussion and in May with a narrowed list and polling direction.
